title: KL10 Model-B production microcode
summary: Use the recovered production microcode for instruction sequences where the architectural manual does not expose the exact restart, parity-wait, or special-case implementation behavior.
procedure: Locate the instruction micro-routine, then follow shared transfer/memory subroutines before inferring a CPU-visible result.
Treat restart/fixup labels as evidence about what architectural state must be reconstructable after a fault or interrupt.
For BLT, distinguish the normal copy loop from the explicit clear-core optimization.
invariants: Microcode explains implementation sequencing; it does not license simulator shortcuts that alter architected state.
BLT clear-core optimization and general BLT must remain distinct paths.
Fault restart state must be reconstructed as the microcode expects, not from host-loop convenience.
